name: The verb in the passive (al-majhūl)
definition: The verb whose doer is not named, built for its object: in the past with u on the first letter and i before the last (nuṣira), in the present with u on the prefix and a before the last (yunṣaru).
body: The books call it the verb 'built for the unknown' (al-mabnī li-l-majhūl) or 'for the object' (li-l-mafʿūl), and the noun that takes the doer's place the nāʾib al-fāʿil. Its forms are made from the active by changing the vowels, and every bāb gives the same pattern; the engine of the conjugation tables makes them from the active verb.

examples.text: nuṣira, yunṣaru: the passive of naṣara.
ḍuriba, yuḍrabu: the passive of ḍaraba.
